chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man in ihram who had intercourse with his wife, so he said: 'If he was ignorant, there is no penalty upon him; but if he was not ignorant, then upon him is to bring a camel and they are separated until they complete the rituals and return to the place where they committed what they committed, and upon them is the Hajj next year.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or 'Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a man in ihram who has intercourse with his wife?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific expiation (*kaffarah*) for sexual intercourse during Hajj, distinguishing between ignorance and knowledge as key determinants of liability. The ruling requires the husband to sacrifice a camel and remain separated from his wife until both complete their respective Hajj rituals, ensuring the validity of the current pilgrimage before returning for the next year. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of ritual purity and the distinct obligations of the husband and wife in such cases.
